extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: A focused set of definitions, theorems, and criteria for computing depth, recognizing Cohen–Macaulay rings/schemes, applying the Miracle Flatness criterion, and applying Serre's R1+S2 criterion for normality. Intended to guide proofs and verifications about depth, regular sequences, flatness, and normality in Noetherian local rings and finite-type schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth computation via non-zerodivisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute depth by successively finding non-zerodivisors in m: (a) if no non-zerodivisor in m exists then depth M = 0; (b) otherwise choose such x and replace M by M/xM and repeat. The process must terminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Exercise 28.1.A, 28.1.B and 28.1.4. Use Theorem 28.1.2 for the step depth(M/xM)=depth M−1. The termination of the process is assured by Exercise 28.1.B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth drops by one under a non-zerodivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a non-zerodivisor in m on a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian local ring (A,m), then depth(M/xM) = depth M − 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: Exercise 28.1.E. Hint given: use Theorem 28.1.2. This is the key local inductive step in depth computations and slicing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound on depth by dimensions of associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth of a module M is at most the smallest dim A/p as p runs over the associated prime ideals of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 28.1.6. The example of two planes meeting at a point shows the bound need not be sharp. The proof uses Lemma 28.1.7 (Ischebeck lemma) and exercises referenced in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ischebeck Ext-vanishing lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose (A,m) is Noetherian local, and M,N are nonzero finitely generated A-modules. Then Ext^i_A(N,M)=0 for i < depth M − dim Supp N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 28.1.7. The proof is inductive on dim Supp N and uses long exact Ext sequences and Nakayama's lemma; it is used to deduce depth bounds (Theorem 28.1.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Cohen–Macaulay (local ring and scheme)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian local ring (A,m) is Cohen–Macaulay if depth A = dim A. A locally Noetherian scheme is Cohen–Macaulay if all of its local rings are Cohen–Macaulay. Equivalently, A is Cohen–Macaulay if all localizations A_p at primes p are Cohen–Macaulay (Spec A Cohen–Macaulay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 28.2.1. Remarks clarify local vs global versions and that localization preserves Cohen–Macaulayness (Fact 28.2.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen–Macaulay implies equidimensionality and no embedded points
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring, then Spec A is equidimensional and has no embedded points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 28.2.B. Note the warning: the converse is false in general (a Noetherian local ring of pure dimension with no embedded primes need not be Cohen–Macaulay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing criterion for Cohen–Macaulayness
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose (A,m) is Noetherian local and x ∈ m is a non-zerodivisor. Then A is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if A/(x) is Cohen–Macaulay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 28.2.3. This gives an inductive way to check Cohen–Macaulayness by slicing by non-zerodivisors; compare to slicing criteria for regularity and flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric slicing interpretation (Cartier divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a locally Noetherian scheme and D an effective Cartier divisor, then: if X is Cohen–Macaulay then D is Cohen–Macaulay; conversely, if D is Cohen–Macaulay then X is Cohen–Macaulay at the points of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary/interpretation of Theorem 28.2.3 (28.2.4). Use this to reason about CM behavior under taking divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular-sequence characterization in Cohen–Macaulay rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m) is Cohen–Macaulay, then a set x1,...,xr ∈ m is a regular sequence for A if and only if dim A/(x1,...,xr) = dim A − r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 28.2.D. This ties algebraic regular sequences to the expected dimension drop, simplifying many dimension-based checks in CM rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m) is a regular local ring (Noetherian by definition here), then A is Cohen–Macaulay; equivalently depth A = dim A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise/Fact referenced in 28.2.5 and 28.1.F. This justifies that smooth schemes over a field are Cohen–Macaulay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular embeddings in smooth k-schemes are Cohen–Macaulay
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular embeddings in smooth k-schemes are Cohen–Macaulay (and hence have no embedded points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 28.2.6 and subsequent remarks. Useful geometric consequence used elsewhere in the text (e.g., Exercise references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracle Flatness (algebraic criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose φ : (B,n) → (A,m) is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with A Cohen–Macaulay, B regular, and the fiber A ⊗_B (B/n) has pure dimension dim A − dim B. Then φ is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 28.2.10. Proof by induction on dim B using slicing and Cohen–Macaulay properties; an algebraic version of the geometric Miracle Flatness theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracle Flatness (geometric criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is a morphism of equidimensional finite-type k-schemes where X is Cohen–Macaulay, Y is regular, and the fibers of π have pure dimension dim X − dim Y. Then π is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 28.2.11 (geometric formulation). See Exercise 28.2.F for a proof and 28.2.G for related equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-of-three criterion linking flatness, X Cohen–Macaulay, and Cohen–Macaulay fibers
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y with X,Y equidimensional and Y regular, any two of the following imply the third: (i) π is flat of relative dimension dim X − dim Y; (ii) X is Cohen–Macaulay; (iii) every fiber X_y is Cohen–Macaulay of pure dimension dim X − dim Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 28.2.G. Note: in the implication (ii) and (iii) imply (i), the Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis in (iii) may be weakened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and localization preservation of Cohen–Macaulayness
rubrics_metrics.description: The locus of Cohen–Macaulay points of a locally Noetherian scheme is open. Any localization of a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring at a prime is Cohen–Macaulay. Moreover, A is Cohen–Macaulay iff A[x] (and A[[x]]) is Cohen–Macaulay; completion preserves Cohen–Macaulayness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28.2.13 and Fact 28.2.14. Consequences: for quasicompact schemes CM may be checked at closed points; CM is preserved under polynomial/power-series extension and completion (references given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of properties R_k and S_k
rubrics_metrics.description: R_k: A is regular in codimension k if for every prime p of codimension ≤ k, A_p is regular. S_k: for every prime p, depth A_p ≥ min(k, dim A_p) (i.e., local rings are Cohen–Macaulay up to codimension k and have depth at least k thereafter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 28.3.1. These properties generalize notions of being generically reduced (R0) and having no embedded points (S1) and are used in Serre's criterion for normality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's criterion for normality (R1 + S2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian ring A is normal (all localizations A_p are integrally closed domains) if and only if it has properties R1 and S2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 28.3.2. Consequences: Cohen–Macaulay schemes are normal iff regular in codimension 1, and this gives concrete checks for normality of hypersurfaces and regular embeddings. Examples and cautionary notes follow (e.g., examples satisfying R1 but not S2).

rubrics_metrics.name: S2 must be checked at all primes (not just up to codimension 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The S2 condition is a condition on all prime ideals, not only on those of codimension at most 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution 28.3.6 and Exercise 28.3.E: there are varieties satisfying R1 and Cohen–Macaulay at points of codimension ≤ 2 which are nevertheless not normal because S2 fails at higher-codimension primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are integrally closed (via R1 + S2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular local rings are integrally closed: regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay and regular in codimension 1, hence normal (integrally closed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application 28.3.5: this gives a route to integral closedness of regular local rings via Serre's criterion rather than deeper theorems; references to earlier facts are given.
